before: The four points are already centered. The centered Gram matrix is $B=\begin{pmatrix}1/2&0&-1/2&0\\0&1/2&0&-1/2\\-1/2&0&1/2&0\\0&-1/2&0&1/2\end{pmatrix}$. The unit vector $u_x=(-1,1,1,-1)^T/2$ is an eigenvector with eigenvalue $1$, as is $u_y=(-1,-1,1,1)^T/2$; the other two eigenvalues are zero. Thus the x-coordinate choice $Y_M=u_x$ is a valid q=1 classical-MDS output, and it has repeated pairs $y_1=y_4$ and $y_2=y_3$.

before: Let $X=M+A$ and $Z=N+C$ as in the statement. Stop so that the local martingales and total variations of $A,C$ are bounded. On every partition the exact identity $\displaystyle X_tZ_t-X_0Z_0=\sum_kX_{t_k}\Delta_k Z+\sum_kZ_{t_k}\Delta_k X+\sum_k\Delta_kX\Delta_kZ$ holds at the terminal time. The first two sums split into the integrals against $M,N$ from step 4.2 and the ordinary Lebesgue–Stieltjes integrals against $A,C$. In the last sum, each cross term containing a finite-variation increment tends to zero, for example $|\sum\Delta_kM\Delta_kC|\le\max_k|\Delta_kM|\operatorname{Var}(C)\to0$ by continuity; the remaining $\sum\Delta_kM\Delta_kN$ converges to $[M,N]$ by steps 3.1–2.2. Passing to the limit proves the displayed product formula on the stopped interval, and localization proves it on $[0,T]$.
